patient_profile.diagnosis_summary: Adult female with chronic migraine, under ongoing neurology care.

request.requested_disposition: Coverage approval for continued Vyepti infusions for chronic migraine prevention

denial_rationale: Insurer denied Vyepti, offering an alternative self-administered CGRP agent (Ajovy) as the plan's preferred preventive therapy.

known_facts.text: Patient has chronic migraine under active neurologic management.
Current preventive regimen includes nerve blocks every 6 weeks, zonisamide, gabapentin, magnesium, and Vyepti infusions.
Concurrent medications include duloxetine, levothyroxine, Nexplanon, spironolactone, and PRN hydroxyzine.

Prior preventive therapies included amitriptyline (no benefit), propranolol and atenolol (discontinued for dropping blood pressure), Aimovig (over 3 months without benefit), and Emgality (4 months without benefit).
Patient self-reports an aversion to needles/injections.

treatment_or_claim_history.description: Trials of amitriptyline, propranolol, atenolol, Aimovig (>3 months), and Emgality (4 months), each without adequate benefit or due to side effects.
Started on Vyepti infusions as part of current preventive regimen.

available_evidence.description: Neurology visit notes documenting current and prior preventive regimens
Documentation of formal trial of Ajovy (plan's preferred self-administered CGRP agent)

unknowns: Whether a formal trial of Ajovy specifically (as opposed to Aimovig and Emgality) has been attempted.
Whether the needle aversion has a documented clinical basis beyond self-report.
